Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper presents an original research study focused on simulating future land use/land cover (LULC) changes at the national scale of China. It explicitly implements spatially explicit modeling across the entire country using a 10 km resolution grid. The primary objective is to project and compare LULC dynamics under two distinct future scenarios (Scenario A: increasing grain yield; Scenario B: constant yield), directly addressing LULC prediction as the central research question. The integrated model couples socioeconomic drivers, ecosystem processes, and land allocation, producing mapped projections for 2020, 2050, and 2080. Quantitative results include area changes (e.g., cropland decreases by 27.37% in Scenario A vs. increases by 29.41% in Scenario B by 2080), conversion matrices derived from Markov chain analysis (2000–2005), and model validation against observed 2010 land use data (Figure 3). All core inclusion criteria are met: national-scale spatial implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatial modeling with accuracy/validation metrics, and mapped LULC outputs. None of the exclusion criteria apply—the study is not global without disaggregation, not regional/local, includes explicit LULC prediction, and is not methodological, qualitative, or single-scenario.)
